decisive_items: small superior sinus tract without obvious pits and mild serous discharge
The lesion was located more than 5 cm from the anal verge
6 × 13 × 28 mm area of nonspecific, irregular superficial enhancement in the natal cleft without invasion of underlying structures
response.rationale: A chronic sinus in the natal cleft located more than 5 cm from the anal verge, with serous discharge and no abscess cavity or metastasis, best fits an indolent pilonidal disease rather than SCC, PG, HS, or a pressure ulcer. The psoriasis-like plaques remain background inflammatory skin change.

rejected.why: No clear immobility or pressure mechanism is given, and the plaque/sinus picture is not typical of a pressure ulcer.
No exophytic or invasive mass and no nodal/distant metastasis; the enhancement is nonspecific, making SCC a less-supported first-line diagnosis.
The lesion lacks a undermined violaceous ulcer edge or associated systemic/inflammatory-comorbidity pattern typical of pyoderma gangrenosum.
No recurrent abscesses/nodules/comedones typical of hidradenitis suppurativa, and the serous sinus with psoriatic plaque is insufficiently specific.
